name: Mohamed Moheyeldin
headline: Senior SDET | Test Automation Lead | Quality Engineering
summary: Hands-on Software Development Engineer in Test and quality engineering leader with 10+ years of experience designing scalable UI and API automation, building reliable test frameworks, integrating quality signals into delivery pipelines, and applying local and cloud AI across federal, e-commerce, and banking environments.
detailedSummary: Senior Software Development Engineer in Test and Test Automation Lead with 10+ years of experience delivering scalable, reliable software across federal, banking, e-commerce, and enterprise environments. Specialized in UI, API, integration, and end-to-end automation using Playwright, Cypress, Selenium WebDriver, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Cucumber BDD, REST Assured, and Postman.

Combines hands-on framework engineering with technical leadership: defining test strategy, automation roadmaps, framework standards, risk-based testing, release-readiness criteria, and quality engineering practices while remaining active in development, debugging, code review, test implementation, and failure analysis.

Uses ChatGPT, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, and local language models for development, test design, debugging, documentation, code review, and daily engineering tasks, with human verification and automated quality gates protecting the final result.

experience.title: QA Test Engineer
experience.summary: Hands-on automation engineering and technical leadership in federal delivery environments, guiding framework direction while improving the quality signals teams use to make release decisions.
highlights: Led a team of five automation engineers, establishing scalable test strategies, resource planning, and automation standards.
Designed Cypress and Playwright frameworks for UI and API testing with resilient asynchronous handling, retry logic, and robust assertions.

Built GitHub Actions pipelines that distributed Cypress Dashboard and Playwright workloads across multiple virtual machines, managed artifacts, and provisioned environments dynamically for faster, diagnosable feedback.
Used AWS EC2, Aurora DB, and S3 to support on-demand test environments and scalable test execution.
Implemented automated defect triage through Jira API integration and risk-based failure prioritization.
Created test dashboards with Allure and Elastic Stack for trend analysis, failure-pattern recognition, and anomaly detection.
Balanced parallel workloads using suite composition and observed execution time, then tracked worker timing, retries, failure categories, artifact completeness, and environment health.
Developed data-provisioning utilities using JSON, Excel with Apache POI, and SQL-driven injection for mock responses and contract testing.
Configured Selenium Grid for parallel cross-browser testing and JMeter performance benchmarks.

Used Cypress Dashboard duration, failure, retry, video, and screenshot evidence to diagnose bottlenecks and tune parallel execution.

aiPractice.title: Local-First AI Engineering Orchestrator
aiPractice.summary: An active local-first AI engineering system that decomposes complex work into specialized subtasks, routes each subtask to the model best suited to the problem and available hardware, runs independent work in parallel, and synthesizes the results into one verified response.
highlights: Designed an orchestration layer that classifies requests, decomposes complex work, routes subtasks by capability and hardware cost, and merges parallel agent results into one traceable answer.
Built a Git-aware repository indexer that detects working-tree and remote-branch changes, incrementally refreshes affected files, and preserves project knowledge between AI sessions.
Created a retrieval-augmented context layer combining semantic embeddings, keyword recall, file metadata, symbols, dependencies, tests, and change history.
Prepared compact, source-linked context packets locally before selective escalation to ChatGPT, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Copilot, or another cloud service.
Applied AI across frontend development, automation framework design, test generation, debugging, code review, documentation, failure analysis, and daily engineering workflows.
Designed local-first fallbacks so routine work can continue without usage quotas while sensitive repository context remains on the workstation unless a deliberate cloud handoff is required.
Experimented with GGUF model packaging, quantization, llama.cpp, Ollama, ONNX Runtime, and OpenVINO to balance memory use, throughput, latency, and response quality.
Added verification stages that compare agent conclusions with source files, tests, and command output before synthesized results are accepted.

projects.name: Portfolio & Career Content System
projects.description: A schema-driven Astro platform that keeps the website portfolio, browser resume, and generated PDF and DOCX outputs aligned through one validated professional data source.
projects.challenge: Career facts had to remain consistent across a public website, browser resume, concise application resume, and detailed technical resume without duplicating content or weakening presentation quality.
approach: Designed a schema-validated career record consumed by every presentation channel.
Built accessible, responsive Astro pages with zero client-framework runtime.
Generated separate PDF and DOCX formats from the same factual source while preserving channel-appropriate layout.
Added strict diagnostics, browser journeys, accessibility analysis, and continuous deployment.
projects.outcome: Established one maintainable publishing workflow for the portfolio and resume library while keeping web, PDF, and Word presentations aligned.
highlights: Designed one structured content architecture for every career presentation channel.
Built accessible, responsive pages with zero client-framework runtime.
Added strict diagnostics, browser journeys, automated accessibility analysis, and continuous deployment.
Prepared separate PDF and DOCX presentation contracts without duplicating career facts.
